intro: Boston rewards visitors with colonial streets, world-class museums and a lively waterfront. Pick how long you have and what you enjoy most.
tour_note: Check the tour page for which entry tickets are included.

notes: The T subway has four colour-coded lines; the Blue Line links the airport area to downtown.
The Silver Line bus runs free from Logan to South Station and connects to the Red Line.
Buses and the subway use a CharlieCard; tap or buy at stations.
Taxis are mostly white and cost $25-50 from Logan to downtown.
Uber and Lyft pick up and drop off at Logan; check the current pickup zone.
Central Boston is compact and walkable; bikes and ferries serve the harbour.

faneuil-hall.name: Faneuil Hall Marketplace
faneuil-hall.price_text: Free to walk; food and shops extra
faneuil-hall.hours: Marketplace roughly 10:00–21:00 daily; check on the day
faneuil-hall.tip: Start at Quincy Market for food stalls, then walk to the historic hall behind it.

uss-constitution.name: USS Constitution
uss-constitution.price_text: Free; ID needed for adults at the gate
uss-constitution.hours: Tue–Sun roughly 10:00–16:00; closed Mondays; check on the day
uss-constitution.tip: Bring photo ID for all adults. The ship is in Charlestown, a short walk from the North End.

baskin-robbins.name: Baskin-Robbins
baskin-robbins.hours: Varies by branch; most open late morning to evening
baskin-robbins.tip: A quick, cheap ice-cream stop; branches are all over the city, so use the nearest one.

boston-college.name: Boston College
boston-college.hours: Campus grounds open daily; buildings vary
boston-college.tip: It is outside the city centre in Chestnut Hill; go only if you have a reason, such as a campus visit.

duck-tours.name: Boston Duck Tours
duck-tours.price_text: ≈ $45–55 adult; child rates lower; book ahead
duck-tours.hours: Departures roughly 09:00–dusk, seasonal; check on the day
duck-tours.tip: Book online in advance and arrive 20 minutes early; the ride ends with a splash into the Charles River.

public-library.name: Boston Public Library
public-library.hours: Mon–Thu roughly 09:00–21:00, Fri–Sat shorter, Sun afternoon; check on the day
public-library.tip: Do not miss the Italian courtyard and the Bates Hall reading room upstairs.

boston-university.name: Boston University
boston-university.tip: The campus stretches along Commonwealth Avenue; the walk down the avenue is the main sight.

brandeis.name: Brandeis University
brandeis.tip: It is in Waltham, well outside Boston; skip unless you are visiting someone there.

charles-river.name: Charles River Esplanade
charles-river.tip: Walk or rent a bike along the river path; the view back to Back Bay is best near sunset.

dunkin.name: Dunkin'
dunkin.hours: Many branches open early to late; hours vary
dunkin.tip: Cheap breakfast on the go; branches are everywhere downtown, so pick the nearest.

harvard.name: Harvard University
harvard.price_text: Free to walk; Harvard Yard open to visitors
harvard.hours: Yard open daily; some buildings need a student guide
harvard.tip: Start in Harvard Yard, then walk through Harvard Square for coffee and bookshops.

mit.name: Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT)
mit.hours: Campus open daily; some buildings restricted
mit.tip: Walk along the Charles from MIT for the best view of the Boston skyline.

aquarium.name: New England Aquarium
aquarium.price_text: ≈ $30–40 adult; child rates lower; book a timed ticket
aquarium.hours: Daily roughly 09:00–17:00, later in summer; check on the day
aquarium.tip: Book a timed entry online and go early; the giant ocean tank is the highlight.

northeastern.name: Northeastern University
northeastern.tip: A short walk from the Museum of Fine Arts; combine the two if you are in the area.

old-north-church.name: Old North Church
old-north-church.price_text: ≈ $8–12 for the church and crypt tour; check on the day
old-north-church.hours: Roughly 10:00–17:00, seasonal; check on the day
old-north-church.tip: Pair it with a walk through the North End for pastries on the same street.

sam-adams-brewery.name: Samuel Adams Brewery
sam-adams-brewery.price_text: ≈ $10–15 tour with tasting; check on the day
sam-adams-brewery.hours: Tours most days, afternoon and evening; book ahead
sam-adams-brewery.tip: It is in Jamaica Plain, a short ride from downtown; book a tour slot online.

symphony-hall.name: Symphony Hall
symphony-hall.price_text: ≈ $30–100+ depending on the concert; some cheap seats
symphony-hall.hours: Show times vary; box office daytime
symphony-hall.tip: Check the Boston Symphony Orchestra schedule and book the cheapest upper seats for good sound.

trinity-church.name: Trinity Church
trinity-church.price_text: ≈ $8–12 donation or entry; check on the day
trinity-church.tip: Step inside for the painted interior, then look back at it from Copley Square.

tufts.name: Tufts University
tufts.tip: It is in Medford, outside the city; only worth it for a campus visit.

harbor-cruise.name: USS Constitution Harbor Cruise
harbor-cruise.price_text: ≈ $30–40 adult; child rates lower; check on the day
harbor-cruise.hours: Seasonal departures, spring to autumn; check on the day
harbor-cruise.tip: Sit on the open deck for skyline views; bring a jacket, it is cooler on the water.

watson-shark.name: Watson and the Shark (John Singleton Copley painting)
watson-shark.price_text: ≈ $25–30 museum entry; check on the day
watson-shark.hours: Museum of Fine Arts roughly 10:00–17:00, closed some days; check on the day
watson-shark.tip: The painting hangs at the Museum of Fine Arts; check the gallery before you go.

quincy-market-food.name: Quincy Market food hall
quincy-market-food.hours: Roughly 10:00–21:00 daily; check on the day
quincy-market-food.tip: Good for a quick, varied lunch; it gets crowded at midday, so go early or late.

skywalk-view.name: Skywalk Observatory viewpoint
skywalk-view.price_text: ≈ $20–30; check current opening and price on the day
skywalk-view.hours: Check on the day; some observatories close seasonally
skywalk-view.tip: Go on a clear day for views over the Back Bay and the river.

freedom-trail-walk.name: Freedom Trail walk
freedom-trail-walk.price_text: Free to walk; some sites charge entry
freedom-trail-walk.hours: Always open; sites have their own hours
freedom-trail-walk.tip: Follow the red brick line from Boston Common to Charlestown; wear comfortable shoes.

beacon-hill-walk.name: Beacon Hill and Acorn Street walk
beacon-hill-walk.hours: Always open; it is a residential street
beacon-hill-walk.tip: Acorn Street is tiny and lived in; keep quiet and do not block doorways for photos.

seaport-walk.name: Seaport waterfront walk
seaport-walk.tip: Walk the harbour edge at sunset, then eat at the nearby food spots.

north-end-food-walk.name: North End food walk
north-end-food-walk.hours: Shops and bakeries roughly 08:00–20:00; check on the day
north-end-food-walk.tip: Try a cannoli and a slice of pizza; the side streets are quieter than Hanover Street.

stays.why: Walk to the Freedom Trail, Faneuil Hall and the aquarium. Best base for a first visit.
Pretty streets, shopping on Newbury Street and easy T rides to the centre.
Quiet brick lanes next to Boston Common and the State House; small inns and guesthouses.
New waterfront hotels, harbour views and the ICA museum; 15–20 minutes' walk to downtown.

food: Try a lobster roll and New England clam chowder; prices vary a lot, so compare menus before you sit down.
Walk the North End for Italian pastries and pasta; it is busy at weekends, so go early or on a weekday.
Faneuil Hall and Quincy Market have many food stalls — handy for groups with different tastes.
For cheap eats, look around Chinatown and the student areas near universities.
Book popular dinner spots ahead, especially in summer and on game nights near Fenway Park.
more_time: Swap a city day for Cambridge: walk or take the Red Line to Harvard Square and the MIT area.
Take a harbour ferry or water taxi for a cheap view of the skyline and the waterfront.
Add a day trip by train to Salem or Providence; check timetables on the day.
